references.text: The immediate context where Moses sets the conditions for Gad and Reuben to settle east of the Jordan—they must first cross over and fight before the Lord.
Moses repeats the conditions for the tribes—if they cross over armed and the land is subdued, they shall receive Gilead as their possession.
Moses reminds the tribes of the agreement—they must help their brothers until the Lord gives them rest and they take possession of the land.
Joshua reminds Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh of the promise they made to Moses to assist in the conquest.
The fulfillment of the promise—Joshua sends the tribes back after the land is subdued and declares them free from their obligation.
A similar concept of being נָקִי (innocent/free)—the guilty one bears the consequences, while the others go free.
David declares himself and his kingdom נָקִי (innocent) in the sight of the Lord regarding Abner's blood.
The spies use similar language about being נְקִיִּם (free from an oath or obligation) toward Rahab.
Pilate declares himself ἀθῷος (innocent) in Jesus' blood—a similar concept of being free from guilt before God and people.
Paul declares himself καθαρός (clean) from the blood of all—this same principle of being free from responsibility before God and people.
